false } }>><<nobr>> <div class="game-intro"> <h1>The Long Summer</h1> <p class="game-description">Maya, eighteen, arrives at her stepfather Frank's rural property in Millhaven, North Alabama, the summer after a revenge beat that collapsed her friend group and ended her relationship. Her mother Diana holds the kitchen at 6:30 and the house by the old code. Outside the screen door, the town runs on a register Diana doesn't enforce. Sixty dollars a week to Frank. Fifteen to groceries. Fifteen hundred to walk onto the community-college campus. Base diner wages don't get her there. Three men live in the house — Frank the landlord with his two-phase arc, Ryan the older stepbrother with a failing shop, and Jake the younger stepbrother who draws what he won't say. Maya lives in both registers at once. The game is how she decides which rules of her old code still apply when the math says otherwise and Diana is still quiet at the table. </p> <div class="developer-intro"> <p class="developer-about">We're a small indie studio crafting intimate, story-driven experiences. Every game is made with care, and your support helps us keep creating. Broad through the shoulders and heavy in the arms — a man who still does the work he used to get paid for. Blunt, calloused hands with a web of small framing scars. Salt-and-pepper hair cut short every four weeks at the barber on Main Street. Crow&#x27;s feet that deepen when he&#x27;s tired, which is more often than he admits. Flannel shirts rolled to the elbow spring through fall, t-shirts when the heat gets above ninety. Jeans that fit. Work boots by the door. Addresses Maya by name — *Maya* — and the name lands like a door closing.</p> <div class="customize-field"> <label>Name</label> <<textbox "$npcs[\"1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d\"].name" "Frank">> </div> <div class="customize-field"> <label>Relationship</label> <<listbox "$npcs[\"1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d\"].relationship" autoselect>> <<option "step-dad" "step-dad">> <<option "mom's husband" "mom's husband">> <<option "landlord" "landlord">> <</listbox>> </div> </div> <div class="customize-npc"> <div class="customize-npc-header"> <img src="./videos/ryan.jpg" alt="Ryan" class="customize-portrait" onerror="this.style.display='none'"> <span class="customize-npc-default-name">Ryan</span> </div> <p class="customize-description">Twenty-five. Lean through the shoulders, strong through the back, tanned to the elbow from yard work. Faint scar across the back of his right forearm from a belt that slipped two years ago. Stretches with his hands laced behind his head after he sets something down — automatic, not performative. Eye contact rare but lands when it does, and holds a count longer than polite when it does. Faded t-shirts washed into softness. Jeans with grease at the knee. Work boots worn soft at the toe. Speaks in fragments. Colloquial. Compliments sideways — *you cleaned up*, not *you look nice*.</p> <div class="customize-field"> <label>Name</label> <<textbox "$npcs[\"e34c78c8-4956-45b8-b021-737ced0d28a0\"].name" "Ryan">> </div> <div class="customize-field"> <label>Relationship</label> <<listbox "$npcs[\"e34c78c8-4956-45b8-b021-737ced0d28a0\"].relationship" autoselect>> <<option "step-brother" "step-brother">> <<option "housemate" "housemate">> <<option "business partner" "business partner">> <</listbox>> </div> </div> <div class="customize-npc"> <div class="customize-npc-header"> <img src="./videos/jake.jpg" alt="Jake" class="customize-portrait" onerror="this.style.display='none'"> <span class="customize-npc-default-name">Jake</span> </div> <p class="customize-description">Twenty-one. Lean, narrower through the shoulder than Ryan. Wrists that look like they could be broken in one grip. Glasses for drawing and reading, off for everything else — a habit he started in high school. Shaggy brown hair falling in his eyes; he pushes it back with the inside of his wrist. Black t-shirts more often than color. Jeans or cargoes, always with a pen in the pocket. Uses doorframes and porch rails to stand against. Flinches at accidental touch. Long sentences when comfortable, clipped when not — vocabulary shows the education he&#x27;s still half-finishing. Draws nude women as his working register, secretly draws Maya once her beauty rises past a threshold he can&#x27;t defend against.</p> <div class="customize-field"> <label>Name</label> <<textbox "$npcs[\"3224c3cf-2963-48ef-bbce-58603f36d71a\"].name" "Jake">> </div> <div class="customize-field"> <label>Relationship</label> <<listbox "$npcs[\"3224c3cf-2963-48ef-bbce-58603f36d71a\"].relationship" autoselect>> <<option "step-brother" "step-brother">> <<option "housemate" "housemate">> <<option "artist roommate" "artist roommate">> <</listbox>> </div> </div> <div class="customize-actions"> [[Continue to Game->StartingCanvas_prologue_morning_with_daniel_Node_1]] </div> </div> <</nobr>> <style> .customize-page { max-width: 600px; He set the phone face-down on his thigh in a gesture she catalogued.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> I didn't know you were coming.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> I didn't know I was coming either. Just needed the night.</div></div><p>He nodded. The house's porch light was behind them and his face was half in shadow and she could see, for the first time really, the shape of his jaw, the place where the stubble came in unevenly on the left side, a small patch of skin above the cheekbone where it didn't grow. He had an old t-shirt on. The t-shirt had a faded logo for a show she had liked in high school and that she hadn't seen him wearing before.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> I liked that band.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Me too. Long time ago.</div></div><p>They sat. The beer on his knee was doing the condensation thing. Somewhere inside the house somebody played the song they always played at parties, the one everyone knew but nobody could remember the name of, and a chorus of voices came up, and died down, and came up again.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Hey. I saw the thing you did. On the wall, by the community center. With the birds.</div></div><p>She looked at him.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Saw it in July, actually. After you told me about it at Adam's thing. I went over.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> You went over.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Yeah. I had to drive past that area for — whatever, doesn't matter. I pulled over. I stood there for ten minutes.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Oh.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> The thing with the — the one bird that's not quite like the others. The one that's looking the wrong way.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Yeah.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Why.</div></div><p>She had known for four months why. It was not a thing she had told Daniel. Daniel had liked the mural, had taken a picture of himself in front of it, had posted it with a caption that said <em>my girl.</em> Daniel had not asked.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Composition. I liked the break in the pattern.</div></div><p>Kevin nodded.</p><p>The truth was that the bird was her. She had painted it looking the wrong way because she had been painting at a time when she had been feeling looked-at in every direction but the one she wanted to be looked in, and the bird was the bird that was not going to be looked at properly because the bird had decided to stop trying. It was the only real thing in the mural. It was the thing she'd been proud of. Kevin had driven over and stood in front of it for ten minutes on a weekday in July and he had asked her the only question anyone had ever asked her about it that mattered.</p><p>She said <em>composition</em> and she watched his face accept the lie without suspicion, because he was the kind of person who took what you said at the value you said it, and this — this was the thing that she was going to carry for the rest of her life without being able to name, the small courtesy of having been told a lie by the person you admired, without ever knowing it had been a lie.</p><p>He drank some of his beer.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Can I get you one?</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Yeah. Please.</div></div><p>He stood up to go inside and she watched the line of his back as he walked through the kitchen, and she noticed that she had already started — the thing she had come here to do had started forty seconds ago and she had not noticed the exact moment it began. That was the part that scared her. Not the doing of it. The not noticing when it began.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "b20f8c7f-1d0b-4607-a765-d8da9873d243">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "dacce178-7713-4106-8cb5-35cc0349a628">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("prologue_morning_with_daniel.party") === -1) { vn.push("prologue_morning_with_daniel.party"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Continue" "StartingCanvas_prologue_morning_with_daniel_Node_7">><<script>>advanceTime(45);<</script>><</link>><br> <</nobr>><div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> The Long Summer — Prologue <span style="opacity:0.7;">(prologue_morning_with_daniel)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> The Guest Bedroom</div> <p>There is a room upstairs in Adam's house that has been a guest bedroom for as long as anyone has been renting the house, a small room with a sloped ceiling that catches the attic heat even in the fall, and which everyone at every party goes up to at some point during the night in pairs or in trios, because the door closes and the lock works and there is a bed and there is a rug and there is one small window that looks out over the neighbor's garage. Maya had been in that room twice before in her life. Once with Sarah, three years ago, who had been crying. Once with Daniel, at a party eleven months ago, which was a thing that she would have to remember later, and was remembering now, as she went up the stairs ahead of Kevin with her hand on the bannister and her left shoe scuffing the second step the way her left shoe always scuffed the second step of old houses.</p><p>The second beer was in her hand. She had not drunk much of it. She had not intended to drink much of it. She had intended to be steady.</p><p>He followed. He had not asked why. That was the part that was making this easier and harder at the same time — she had not given him a reason because she had not needed to. She had gone back out onto the porch after a period of time that he had chosen to read as ambiguous, and she had said <em>come upstairs with me for a minute,</em> and he had said <em>okay</em> the way people say <em>okay</em> when they are agreeing to something they are going to pretend they didn't agree to. He had left his beer on the porch step.</p><p>She opened the door. She closed it behind him. She turned the lock.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> Maya.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Yeah.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> I don't —</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> I know.</div></div><p>He looked at her. There was a single lamp on the nightstand and the lamp was on, because the last people who had been in the room had left it on, and the light was yellow and unkind and the wallpaper in the room was the wrong color for skin — a pale green with a repeating pattern of something that might have been ferns and might have been something else. The pattern was off by a quarter-inch every third repeat. A misprint. The kind of thing Daniel would not have noticed. The kind of thing she had been noticing her whole life.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> What do you know.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Daniel is cheating on me.</div></div><p>Nothing moved in his face except his mouth, slightly. He processed. He was about to say something sympathetic — she watched him find the shape of it — and she spoke before he could.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> With Sarah.</div></div><p>He stopped. She watched him stop.</p><p>For a full breath he was not in the room. Then he was back, and something had rearranged in him — not surprise exactly, because some part of him had always half-known something, the way people always half-know, but the specific naming of it. He set his hand on the dresser to steady it, and the muscle in his forearm shifted the way a muscle shifts when it is absorbing a piece of information that is changing the shape of something it had been arranging.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> How long.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> I don't know. Long enough.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/kevin.jpg" alt="Kevin" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Kevin:</strong> How did you —</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> I saw them.</div></div><p>He did not say anything else for a moment. She watched him arrive at the place she had arrived at on Wednesday afternoon — the place where the facts sat in the center of the room and the old life was on one side of the facts and the new life was on the other and the only way across was through. Kevin was, she understood now, a person who was going to take longer than her to cross. He was going to cross slower. He was also going to cross. She could see the shape of him crossing.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Come here.</div></div><p>He came.</p><p>She put her hand on his wrist first, which was the gesture she had rehearsed, and she watched herself do it and watched it work. His skin was warmer than she had expected. She had known him for two years and had never touched his wrist.</p><p><em>Daniel's wrist.</em> The memory arrived before she could keep it out. The way Daniel's wrist had felt on Sunday morning, the slow one, his hand on her jaw. She closed her eyes for a second and opened them. Kevin was still standing there. Kevin's wrist was under her hand. Kevin, not Daniel. <em>The classroom.</em> Sarah's mouth. The olive backpack against the leg of the desk. The fluorescent flicker. She blinked it away. Kevin was still there.</p><p>She stood up on her toes. She kissed him.</p><p>His mouth was not what Daniel's mouth was. Every mouth in the world was not what Daniel's mouth was, and she realized in that instant that she had been kissing one man for two years and had forgotten that other mouths existed, and Kevin's mouth was a different mouth, softer at the edges, and he kissed her back in a way that was not what she had expected — not hunger, not hesitation, but a kind of careful attentiveness, as if he were trying to read her rather than take something.</p><p>That was the first thing that she had not accounted for.</p><p>She pulled back. When Maya did not fill the silence, Diana did the thing Diana did when she was about to say the useful part.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/diana.jpg" alt="Diana" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Diana:</strong> And there's a community college in Millhaven. Twenty minutes from the house. It's a good one — better than people give it credit for.</div></div><p>Maya closed her eyes.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/diana.jpg" alt="Diana" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Diana:</strong> I'm not telling you what to do, honey. I'm telling you the math. If you transferred in the fall you'd be paying a fraction of what you're paying now. And you'd be living here, so no rent. No food. I'd do your laundry if you let me. You'd come out the other end of this without the debt you've been building up, and you'd still have the degree.</div></div><p>Maya opened her eyes. Her mother had been counting. Her mother had been doing the numbers for her, quietly, over months probably, waiting for a moment she could say them without it sounding like she was asking. This was the moment. Her mother was not asking.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Mom.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/diana.jpg" alt="Diana" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Diana:</strong> It's a place to be, Maya. That's all I'm saying. It's a place to be, and it's a good school, and the summer is long. Think about the school thing when you get here. You don't have to decide on the drive.</div></div><p>Maya did not cry. She had known she was not going to cry when her mother said the thing she had said, because her mother had said it the correct way, which was as a fact rather than as a rescue, and a fact did not require tears. Nothing about Diana's offer was performance. The numbers were real. The room was real. The college was real. The summer was long. The summer could be longer.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Okay. Thank you.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/diana.jpg" alt="Diana" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Diana:</strong> Drive down when you're ready. Whenever that is.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> Okay.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/diana.jpg" alt="Diana" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Diana:</strong> I love you.</div></div><div class="dialog-block dialog-player"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/maya.jpg" alt="You" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>You:</strong> I know.</div></div><p>Diana ended the call the way Diana ended calls, which was without saying goodbye, because Diana believed in ending calls the way you end a conversation in person, by simply stopping. The phone went dark in Maya's hand.</p><p>She packed that night. She packed the way she did everything. In order. The clothes she wore to work. The clothes she slept in. Her sketchbook, which she wrapped in a t-shirt because the spine had been coming loose. Her paints. The one photograph of her father she carried from place to place. She did not pack the dress from Adam's house. The dress was in a black trash bag already, had been in the trash bag since Sunday afternoon, tied at the top, set by the door to go out with the garbage on Wednesday. Wednesday had come and gone and the bag was still there. She picked it up now and she took it down to the dumpster in the alley, and she dropped it in, and she watched it settle between a cardboard box and a bag of something wet, and she walked back upstairs.</p><p>She was in her car by morning.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "b20f8c7f-1d0b-4607-a765-d8da9873d243">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "dda0a53d-e116-4e48-859a-c7971442f5a7">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("prologue_morning_with_daniel.diana") === -1) { vn.push("prologue_morning_with_daniel.diana"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Drive south." "StartingCanvas_prologue_morning_with_daniel_Node_10">><<script>>advanceTime(0);<</script>><</link>><br> <</nobr>><div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> The Long Summer — Prologue <span style="opacity:0.7;">(prologue_morning_with_daniel)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> Southbound</div> <p>The radio died somewhere outside Memphis. She had not been listening to it anyway; it had been on because her hand had reached for the dial out of habit when she got in the car, and she had not bothered to find a station because she had not wanted to hear anything that was going to make her feel a specific thing. When the radio died she did not turn it back on.</p><p>The highway was the highway. Trees, then more trees, then a rest stop with a chain coffee she did not remember buying. Her hands on the wheel were steady in the same way they had been steady on Kevin's belt, which was a correspondence she did not want to notice and noticed anyway.</p><p>She thought about the house she was driving to.</p><p>She had met Frank twice. The first time was at an Easter when she had been fifteen and Diana had been married to him for maybe four months. Frank had been polite and quiet and had made her plate for her without asking how much she wanted, which had been the exact wrong amount, and he had said grace in a way that was not showy but was not negotiable either. The second time had been at a wedding, not his own, and he had worn a suit that fit and shaken Maya's hand like shaking hands mattered. She remembered the texture of his palm — rough in specific places, like he had done things with his hands for a living. She did not remember him speaking more than six sentences to her total.</p><p>Her mother had said the word <em>strict</em> about him exactly once, in a phone call, in a voice that was not complaining. <em>Frank keeps a house,</em> she had said. <em>Dinner's at six-thirty. Chores have owners.</em> That was the phrase that had stayed: <em>chores have owners.</em> Maya understood what it meant and had not, until now, thought about what it would mean to be inside it.</p><p>There were two sons. She had not met either.</p><p>Ryan was the older one. She knew that he worked on something mechanical — an engine shop, a salvage thing, something with a roof and a bay and a cash drawer. Diana had said he was <em>a good kid</em> in the voice Diana used about people she liked, which was measured and undramatic and you had to have known Diana a long time to hear the warmth in. The younger one was Jake. Jake went to a community college somewhere. Diana had said less about him, which might have meant nothing and might have meant Jake was hard to describe.</p><p>Three men in a house she had never been in. One of them her mother's husband. Two of them her mother's husband's sons.</p><p>She tried to picture them at a table.</p><p>She could not.</p><p>What she could picture, and kept picturing, was the shape of a hallway she had not yet seen. The sound a strange house made at night. The way bathroom doors locked differently depending on whose house you were in. The negotiations of breakfast. Whether Frank's two sons were the kind of men who looked at a woman in her pajamas, and whether they were the kind of men who looked and looked away, and whether they were the kind of men who made it her problem either way.</p><p>She thought about the rent. Her mother had said <em>no rent</em> in the phone call; Maya had already done the math on that and had decided she would pay Frank something anyway, because her pride would not sit at his dinner table eating food she had not earned. Whatever he asked, she would pay. If he did not ask, she would leave it on the kitchen counter and they would not discuss it. She had been doing the math on that for most of Kentucky.</p><p>She thought about the thing nobody in Millhaven knew.</p><p>Nobody in that house had any idea what she had done on Saturday night. Nobody there had any way of finding out unless she told them. That was the one mercy in the whole drive, and she was not sure yet whether it was actually a mercy or just a particular kind of pressure she was going to have to carry differently — the pressure of being, for the first time in her life, in a place where she was entirely herself, unwitnessed. Not the girl who wouldn't let her ex see her cry. Not the best friend who had figured out the shape of her own best friend on a desk. Just a nineteen-year-old with a suitcase and a mother who was waiting on a porch.</p><p>She did not know yet which would be harder.</p><p>By the time she was in Frank's county the light was slanting the way it slanted at the end of summer days in places that smelled like pine and heat and the specific rust of dry red earth. She pulled off the highway. She drove the last six miles on a two-lane road. The driveway was not marked. She almost missed it. She turned in.</p><p>The gravel popped under her tires.</p><div style="border:2px dashed #666;padding:20px;margin:10px 0;border-radius:8px;background:#f5f5f5;"><p style="margin:0;font-weight:bold;color:#333;">[IMAGE MISSING] prologue/n9_driveway.jpg</p><p style="margin:5px 0 0;color:#666;font-style:italic;">A gravel driveway through pines. The house at the end. The light at the end of a summer day in a place that smells like red earth.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=gravel+driveway+through+pines+rural+house+sunset+south&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=prologue%2Fn9_driveway.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 gravel driveway through pines rural house sunset south</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=southern+farmhouse+end+of+long+gravel+drive+summer+evening&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=prologue%2Fn9_driveway.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 southern farmhouse end of long gravel drive summer evening</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=country+home+property+arrival+late+afternoon+red+earth&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=prologue%2Fn9_driveway.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 country home property arrival late afternoon red earth</a></div></div><p>The house stood at the end of the driveway.</p><p>She had one thing to do before she turned the engine off.</p><p>Her phone was in the cup holder. Sarah's name was in her contacts, still, which was its own specific kind of fact. She picked up the phone. She held it. She looked at the house through the windshield and she thought about the currency of the friendship she had spent, and about Sarah's careful paragraphs, and about the three words she had been turning over in her head for most of the drive.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "b20f8c7f-1d0b-4607-a765-d8da9873d243">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "ba397622-41f3-4a19-be02-48ac16217c83">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("prologue_morning_with_daniel.drive") === -1) { vn.push("prologue_morning_with_daniel.drive"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Leave Sarah a voicemail. By Wednesday afternoon she was neither. The third door on the third floor of the Humanities building opened onto Daniel and Sarah, and neither of them looked up, and she closed the door quietly and walked out of the building and sat on a bench outside the library for fifteen minutes without opening her sketchbook. She did not cry. She did not call. She did not confront. She went home and locked the door behind her with the specific care of a person handling something breakable and sat on her bed with her coat still on and made a list in her head, and the fourth item on the list was the one she picked.</p><p>On Saturday night she was at a housewarming in a dress she had not worn yet, sitting on the edge of a bed upstairs with Sarah's boyfriend's hand at her waist. She had thought she might not be able to go through with it. It turned out she could. Kevin broke up with Sarah on Monday morning. By Tuesday evening Daniel had called her and she had let it go to voicemail. By Wednesday Sarah had stopped calling and started writing — long careful paragraphs about feelings and about Daniel and about how the three of them had been, in some rare fictional telling, equally complicated. Maya read the paragraphs once each and did not respond. By Thursday the group chat had gone quiet. A post she made on Instagram in the afternoon got six likes — her mother, her aunt, two bots, a girl from her art class who was always three steps behind on social information, and Kevin.</p><p>On Thursday Diana called. Her mother was not a person who called without a reason. Diana said the house was big and Frank's two sons were home for the summer but there was a room. Diana said the community college in Millhaven was twenty minutes from the house and better than people gave it credit for. Diana said the summer was long. Diana did the math the way Diana did math — as a fact, not as a rescue — and Maya, who had been raised on the same math, heard it. She packed that night. Sketchbook in a t-shirt. Paints. The one photograph of her father. She did not pack the dress. She drove south through Kentucky and through trees and through the radio dying somewhere outside Memphis. By late afternoon she was on a two-lane road in a county she had been to once, for an Easter, when she was fifteen. The driveway was not marked. She almost missed it. She turned in. The gravel popped under her tires.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "b20f8c7f-1d0b-4607-a765-d8da9873d243">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "3302648b-baa5-47f9-b5bb-c7e32ac40a7f">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("prologue_morning_with_daniel.skip_recap") === -1) { vn.push("prologue_morning_with_daniel.skip_recap"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Stop the car." _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Kitchen</h2> <p>The social hub. Butcher-block counter worn pale at the center. Five chairs at a four-person table — <<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>> added one when Maya moved in. The coffee maker starts at 6 a.m. because <<print $npcs["0304dc6e-c8fa-403d-8dd4-db1655c986e0"].name>> is standing over it. The refrigerator hums loud enough to narrate pauses in conversation. The window above the sink looks out on the back yard. Dinner is at 6:30 because <<print $npcs["0304dc6e-c8fa-403d-8dd4-db1655c986e0"].name>> holds it at 6:30.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("f5dd584c-41bd-4515-bfc4-ba779d7a0662")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("f5dd584c-41bd-4515-bfc4-ba779d7a0662")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave Kitchen->Location_Home]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "92d35c5e-f82a-4b17-b1d4-98ba4f970c52">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("92d35c5e-f82a-4b17-b1d4-98ba4f970c52")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("92d35c5e-f82a-4b17-b1d4-98ba4f970c52")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("92d35c5e-f82a-4b17-b1d4-98ba4f970c52")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Living Room</h2> <p>Television against the long wall. Couch deep enough to lie down on. Lamp <<print $npcs["0304dc6e-c8fa-403d-8dd4-db1655c986e0"].name>> brought from the old house. Coffee table with coasters nobody uses. The porch visible through the front window. <<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>> reads here some evenings when the office gets stale. This is the room where the catch-trigger fires.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("92d35c5e-f82a-4b17-b1d4-98ba4f970c52")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("92d35c5e-f82a-4b17-b1d4-98ba4f970c52")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave Living Room->Location_Home]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "f73b2d47-d4f9-412b-ace1-6c9715260d59">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("f73b2d47-d4f9-412b-ace1-6c9715260d59")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("f73b2d47-d4f9-412b-ace1-6c9715260d59")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("f73b2d47-d4f9-412b-ace1-6c9715260d59")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Bathroom</h2> <p>Shared. One tub/shower, one toilet, one sink, a small window over the tub that opens onto the side yard. A single hook for a towel — <<print $npcs["0304dc6e-c8fa-403d-8dd4-db1655c986e0"].name>> added a second when Maya arrived. Steam hangs after <<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>>'s morning shower for an hour.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("f73b2d47-d4f9-412b-ace1-6c9715260d59")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("f73b2d47-d4f9-412b-ace1-6c9715260d59")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave Bathroom->Location_Home]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "d7f3ebd9-7812-4100-a478-2e48eab925ec">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("d7f3ebd9-7812-4100-a478-2e48eab925ec")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("d7f3ebd9-7812-4100-a478-2e48eab925ec")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("d7f3ebd9-7812-4100-a478-2e48eab925ec")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Maya's Bedroom</h2> <p>Was a guest room. Twin bed against the far wall. Small desk Maya claimed for sketching. Window looks onto the front yard and the driveway. Shares a wall with <<print $npcs["3224c3cf-2963-48ef-bbce-58603f36d71a"].name>>'s room — thin enough that she can hear his keyboard after midnight.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("d7f3ebd9-7812-4100-a478-2e48eab925ec")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("d7f3ebd9-7812-4100-a478-2e48eab925ec")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave Maya's Bedroom->Location_Home]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_home_and_invited", "operator": "is_true"}]})>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "f7f34533-b734-4f61-a7d3-1eda657ff5e7">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("f7f34533-b734-4f61-a7d3-1eda657ff5e7")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("f7f34533-b734-4f61-a7d3-1eda657ff5e7")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("f7f34533-b734-4f61-a7d3-1eda657ff5e7")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Frank's Office</h2> <p>The door stays closed when <<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>> isn't in it. Metal filing cabinets older than the house. A desk facing the window so he can see the yard while working. Paper everywhere — neat piles, but piles. The clerk watches Maya's purchases without comment.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("359fd654-ac26-4631-8477-01b8f0d5359a")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("359fd654-ac26-4631-8477-01b8f0d5359a")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave General Store->Location_Main_Street_Sidewalk]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "bd18e4ea-8d77-446b-aa96-9cb1d82290c7">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("bd18e4ea-8d77-446b-aa96-9cb1d82290c7")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("bd18e4ea-8d77-446b-aa96-9cb1d82290c7")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("bd18e4ea-8d77-446b-aa96-9cb1d82290c7")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Gas Station</h2> <p>Two pumps. Half the rep_road crowd stops by daily.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("bd18e4ea-8d77-446b-aa96-9cb1d82290c7")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("bd18e4ea-8d77-446b-aa96-9cb1d82290c7")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave Gas Station->Location_Main_Street_Sidewalk]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "2bb40dae-9feb-421b-9539-94650aa14413">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("2bb40dae-9feb-421b-9539-94650aa14413")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("2bb40dae-9feb-421b-9539-94650aa14413")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("2bb40dae-9feb-421b-9539-94650aa14413")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Post Office</h2> <p>Small. Open 9–5 Mon–Sat.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("2bb40dae-9feb-421b-9539-94650aa14413")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("2bb40dae-9feb-421b-9539-94650aa14413")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave Post Office->Location_Main_Street_Sidewalk]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "181c39ac-4f20-4fd5-a530-ceda1392793d">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("181c39ac-4f20-4fd5-a530-ceda1392793d")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("181c39ac-4f20-4fd5-a530-ceda1392793d")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("181c39ac-4f20-4fd5-a530-ceda1392793d")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>College Admin Office</h2> <p>One room off Main Street — the community college has a small administrative satellite here for locals who can't make it to campus. The community college campus itself is gated — visible through the gate, not entered in Phase 1.</p> <<= setup.renderNpcPortraits("181c39ac-4f20-4fd5-a530-ceda1392793d")>> <<= setup.renderSoloActivities("181c39ac-4f20-4fd5-a530-ceda1392793d")>> <div class="location-navigation"> <<nobr>><div class="location-nav-grid"><a class="location-card link-internal" data-passage="Location_Community_College_Campus"><div class="location-card-image" style="background-image: url('./videos/locations/college_campus.jpg')"></div><div class="location-card-content"><span class="location-card-name">Community College Campus</span><div class="location-card-indicators"><<if setup.locationHasNewCanvases("01ad23c5-b924-458b-b14d-56393aa1d1c2")>><span class="nav-new-badge">NEW</span><</if>><<if setup.locationHasNewUnlockedChoices("01ad23c5-b924-458b-b14d-56393aa1d1c2")>><span class="nav-unlocked-badge">🔓</span><</if>><<for _npc range setup.getNpcsWithCanvasesAtLocation("01ad23c5-b924-458b-b14d-56393aa1d1c2")>><<if _npc.portrait>><img @src="'./videos/' + _npc.portrait" class="nav-npc-badge" @alt="_npc.name"><</if>><</for>></div></div></a></div><</nobr>> <div class="location-nav-exits"> [[Leave College Admin Office->Location_Main_Street_Sidewalk]]<br> </div> </div> <</if>><<nobr>> <<set $player.current_location = "79ec1e8e-cdce-4419-816e-263af0f4d0db">> <<if not $game_state.visited_locations.includes("79ec1e8e-cdce-4419-816e-263af0f4d0db")>> <<set $game_state.visited_locations.push("79ec1e8e-cdce-4419-816e-263af0f4d0db")>> <</if>> <</nobr>><<set _autoFire = setup.getStoryCanvasRedirect("79ec1e8e-cdce-4419-816e-263af0f4d0db")>><<if _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>Church Front</h2> <p>Maya attends the lawn and the front steps — the parking-lot-to-steps walk is where rep_church accumulates without her entering the sanctuary. _autoFire>><<goto _autoFire>><<else>><h2>The Lake Beach</h2> <p>A stretch of shoreline on the lake twenty minutes out of town. Sand where the shore flattens, scrub pines at the edge, picnic benches that have not been picnicked on this year. Quiet enough that two people talking can hear their own pauses. The sun is high and the water is the color of iron where the bottom drops. Small-town Southern Baptist or Methodist church — clean white clapboard, gravel parking lot half-full with pickup trucks and a handful of sedans, mowed front lawn between the lot and stone front steps, congregation gathering on the lawn for the lawn-to-steps social work before the service interior. The gravel lot half-full with trucks and a handful of sedans. The lawn between the lot and the front steps had been mowed on Friday — Maya knew because she had heard the mower from the house Friday afternoon and knew now what mower it had been. Diana on the path half a step ahead, not looking back, confident the way a woman who had walked this path most Sundays of two decades was confident. Stone-warming-already-at-ten and Sunday-coffee carrying through the front door.</p><<set _bp to random(0, 2)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>The pastor at the top of the steps in his clean black suit, hand out for the hand-shake the way the pastor's hand was out for the hand-shake every Sunday. He said her name first and Diana's name second, which Maya registered. His grip was the grip of a man who shook a hundred hands every Sunday and had calibrated his grip to do no harm. His eyes were on her for the count of one before he was on to the next greeting.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>The Pruitts — the church-couple from two roads over — found Diana before Diana found them. The woman put her hand on Diana's forearm in the way of women who had been putting their hands on each other's forearms since before Maya was born. The man asked after Frank and Diana said the answer she had said to that question every Sunday. Maya stood half a step behind Diana's shoulder and let herself nod when nodded at.</p> <<else>> <p>By the side door three older women were not yet inside, talking the talk that did not need to be talked but was being talked anyway. One of them — silver curls, lavender-soap smell carrying across — caught Maya's eye and gave the windshield-nod from the road, the same nod that meant a thing. Maya gave it back. The woman went back to the not-needed talk.</p> <</if>><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="dialog-content"><strong>NPC:</strong> Maya. The convenience-store side. The cooler at the back, the door's seal coming loose at the bottom corner the way the door's seal had been coming loose at the bottom corner since she had started coming here. A Coke from the cooler. The clerk on the stool by the register named the price without looking up. Fifty cents.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Gas station weekday afternoon. Ryan's truck at pump two, the tailgate down, the back-end loaded with a half-cord of rough-cut pine that had not been there at breakfast. Ryan inside the convenience store paying. Maya stayed at the cooler the count of two breaths, then took the Coke to the front. They paid at separate counts.</p> <<elseif _bp is 2>> <p>Post office. The postmaster knew Diana's box number by the second week and Diana's daughter's by the third. A letter today, from the aunt in Mobile who wrote the same month every summer because the same month every summer was when she remembered Maya's father's birthday. Maya put the letter in the back pocket of her jeans.</p> <<else>> <p>Post office. The postmaster knew Diana's box and Maya's name by then. Today's mail was a flyer for a tractor-pull at the Hayes County Fairgrounds and a coupon for a chain restaurant two towns over. Nothing she had walked the hour to town for, and nothing she could have said she had walked the hour to town for either.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "2f34fd48-5e9a-477e-9833-bf4c137b6cb2">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "9398ad3f-d6a2-4c9b-8a49-ad66a98f9fbe">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("2f34fd48-5e9a-477e-9833-bf4c137b6cb2");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_errands.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_errands.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(20);<</script>> <<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "rep_road", "add", 1.0, false, null);setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>> [[Cross to Route 9. Wooden brochure rack three feet wide on the right wall, four shelves of folded tri-folds. Wooden application desk at the back of the room with two chairs in front of it (neither sat in this morning), the clerk on a wooden stool behind the desk reading paperwork. Coffee mug cooling on the corner of the desk. Late-morning Southern small-town light through a single front window. The community college campus visible through the gate at the end of the block beyond the office. Maya in jeans and a t-shirt approaching the brochure rack.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=small+community+college+admin+satellite+office+brochure+rack+wooden+desk+Southern+small-town&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fcollege_admin.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 small community college admin satellite office brochure rack wooden desk Southern small-town</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=rural+community+college+storefront+one-room+admin+office+brochure+rack+mid-morning+weekday+clerk&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fcollege_admin.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 rural community college storefront one-room admin office brochure rack mid-morning weekday clerk</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=1980s+American+community-college+satellite+office+Main+Street+wooden+brochure+shelves+application+desk+clerk&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fcollege_admin.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 1980s American community-college satellite office Main Street wooden brochure shelves application desk clerk</a></div></div><p>The college admin office was one room off Main Street, the kind of room a community-college satellite occupied when the satellite did not need more than one room. A wooden brochure rack on the right wall, three feet wide, four shelves of folded paper that looked as though they had been folded by the same hand at the same hour for some number of years. An application desk at the back, two chairs in front of it, neither chair sat in this morning. The clerk on a wooden stool behind the desk. Her coffee cooling on the corner of the desk. The paper smell of the un-stocked third shelf in the back of the room.</p><p>Maya stood at the rack and read the headings on the spines. <em>Welcome / Programs / Tuition and Aid / Apply / Visit the Campus.</em> The tri-fold for the summer term sat on the third shelf in three rows, the way the brochures sat in three rows of three because the rack had been stocked at the hour the rack always got stocked. She lifted one off the shelf. The paper was the kind that held a fold for years. The cover photograph was a brick building she would later see through the gate at the end of the block.</p><p>She turned to the desk with the brochure in her hand the way a person turned to a desk to pay for a thing she was not going to pay for. The clerk lifted her eyes once and let them drop again. The clerk said come back when you're ready and did not look up to say it. The voice was the voice of a woman who had said the line to some number of girls at some number of hours of some number of weekday mornings. Maya did not say a thing back. Saying a thing back was not the line the clerk had asked for.</p><p>Outside the office the sidewalk was the sidewalk it had been ten minutes earlier. The college campus was visible through the gate at the end of the block — brick, a quad, a building with a window that might have been the art building she had read about on shelf one, in the brochure now folded into the back pocket of her jeans. The fold-line went where the fold-line on the rack-shelf brochures had gone. The math she would do later was already a thing the brochure had handed her without saying so.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "080449c1-9c89-47a7-8d94-3b8e4f34efba">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "23d6c70f-fad9-4592-a20d-e47bde954e2b">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("080449c1-9c89-47a7-8d94-3b8e4f34efba");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_college_admin.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_college_admin.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(30);<</script>> <<script>>setup.applyAndNotifyFlag("player", null, "college_brochure_taken");<</script>> [[Brochure in the back pocket. Old metal cooler humming at the back wall. Old brass cash register on a wooden counter near the front, the clerk on a stool beside it. Cardboard boxes stacked behind the counter. A penny-candy rack near the door. Maya in jeans and a t-shirt at the counter or in one of the aisles. Late-spring afternoon light through the front display window.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=small-town+general+store+interior+wooden+shelves+brass+cash+register+Southern+three-generations+family-run&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fgeneral_store.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 small-town general store interior wooden shelves brass cash register Southern three-generations family-run</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=1980s+American+rural+general+store+cooler+humming+cardboard+boxes+hardware+odds+and+ends+penny+candy+rack&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fgeneral_store.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 1980s American rural general store cooler humming cardboard boxes hardware odds and ends penny candy rack</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=Southern+country+store+interior+wooden+shelves+dry+goods+women%27s+essentials+clerk+stool+front+counter&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fgeneral_store.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 Southern country store interior wooden shelves dry goods women&#x27;s essentials clerk stool front counter</a></div></div><<set _bp to random(0, 2)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>Weekday afternoon. The clerk on the stool by the register reading the Hayes County paper folded to the obituaries. The store had been three families in three generations; the clerk was the second-oldest of the third. The store was hers at this hour and she did not look up when the door bell went.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>The church couple at the canned-goods aisle, whispering at the labels the way they whispered at the diner over the Saturday-morning coffee. The wife had a hand on a can of green beans; the husband's basket was heavier than what the basket should have held. Maya took the next aisle over.</p> <<else>> <p>A kid at the candy rack with hair still wet from the creek, a fistful of penny-candy wrappers he was deciding between. The clerk watched the kid's hands. The kid was six and had not yet learned that the clerk's silence was a kind of wait. Maya remembered that wait from a counter in a different town.</p> <</if>><p>The cooler in the back was running. The cardboard smell sat in the air the way the cardboard sat on the shelves it had been delivered in. The clerk's eye on Maya was the clerk's eye on every customer — no comment, no narrowing — the third generation's house rule. Paper, folded twice at the top, stapled. Marge had cooked too much of whatever didn't sell on the Friday rush; what didn't sell came home with Maya by Saturday afternoon under the deal Frank had made. A week of dinners for the table.</p><<set _bp to random(0, 2)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>Meatloaf week. The slab wrapped in foil that had been folded twice, the way Marge folded foil so the heat-grease did not bleed through the paper. Cornbread in a smaller paper bundle on top, still warm enough that it had softened the bag's bottom corner. Maya carried it home along the gravel shoulder of Route 9.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Chicken-fried-steak week. Two slabs because Marge had cut three off the line and one had gone home with Cookie's older. Gravy in a separate styrofoam cup with the lid taped. Mashed potatoes in the bottom of the bag the way a paper bag held a thing that wanted to leak. Maya did not tilt the bag.</p> <<else>> <p>Pot-roast week. The roast in foil, the carrots and onions in their own paper twist, the broth in a deli container Marge had labeled DINNER in pencil that would smudge by the time Maya got home. Marge tipped her chin once at the door. The bag stayed warm against Maya's hip the hour back to Frank's.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "3fa474cd-b239-439e-85ae-80fad5d1bdb3">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "ad37823e-2344-4a80-a80c-403ca607375d">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("3fa474cd-b239-439e-85ae-80fad5d1bdb3");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_diner_groceries.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_diner_groceries.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(15);<</script>> [[The bag in both hands. Coca-Cola wall clock above the pass. Owner Marge at the till with the credit slips, not looking up. Cookie visible at the grill behind the pass, spatula in left hand, tongs in right. The pebbled-glass of water and the heavy coffee mug Marge had filled before Maya was halfway to the seat. The off-shift register was its own register — apron-not-on, hands-free-of-the-rag — and Maya did not yet know its full shape. Cookie at the grill, spatula in the left hand, tongs in the right. Marge tipped her chin from the credit slips without looking up. The nod was the whole hello.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "cookie_peer_established", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>Cookie clocked her over the pass and went back to the eight-top's hashbrowns without losing the count. The first two weeks had taught Maya the math of Cookie's silences — the silences were attention, the words came when they were earned. Marge poured the second half of the cup at a count Maya had not started counting. The credit slips on the counter went on being credit slips.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "cookie_peer_established", "operator": "is_true"}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "marge_thursday_key", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>At the lull Cookie wiped her hands on the apron front and came around to the customer side of the counter — the one place she was allowed off the line and still inside. Bill'll land at twenty-eight, tip'll be eight, they'll think it's generous. Heads up so you don't waste the line.</div></div> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "marge_thursday_key", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>The cup had been filled before Maya had asked. Marge's nod from the till was the same nod and not the same nod — same mechanics; the weight in it added the night Maya took the key. Cookie tipped her chin from the grill once, mouth flat.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/cookie.jpg" alt="Cookie" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Cookie:</strong> Get yours.</div></div><p>Cookie went back to the line. Private, quiet, the dinner rush long over.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=small-town+Southern+diner+after+close+late+night+corner+back+booth+warm+lamp+private&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fdiner_t3.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 small-town Southern diner after close late night corner back booth warm lamp private</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=1980s+American+diner+late-night+scene+locked+door+single+lit+booth+waitress+and+customer&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fdiner_t3.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 1980s American diner late-night scene locked door single lit booth waitress and customer</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=roadside+diner+closed+for+the+night+back+booth+lamp+young+woman+and+regular&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fdiner_t3.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 roadside diner closed for the night back booth lamp young woman and regular</a></div></div><<set _bp to random(0, 3)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>The Thursday was the scrapper's Thursday. He came in at nine-forty in the white short-sleeve he wore the weeks he had been paid on a Wednesday wire transfer, the one with the snap-pockets; his rig in the gravel turnout since seven, his second cup of coffee since then, the bill he had folded in half and kept under the saltshaker since nine-thirty. Marge at the till had not said anything. Marge at the till did not need to.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>The Thursday was the anniversary-husband's Thursday. He had been at the anniversary dinner a month back and had tipped with the kind of intention a man tipped with when he was setting the next move up. He had come back alone on the two Thursdays since. Tonight he sat in the corner booth with the hat on the seat beside him. Twenty-one-twenty-five on the Coca-Cola clock.</p> <<elseif _bp is 2>> <p>The Thursday was Dale's Thursday. Dale drove the flatbed between Nashville and Chattanooga twice a week and took his Thursday at the diner because the Thursday diner was on his route south. He had eaten a chicken-fried steak and had paid for it twice — once on the bill and once with the twenty he left under the plate on his way to the back booth. Cookie at the pass pretended not to see him leave.</p> <<else>> <p>The Thursday was the kind of Thursday when the man in the booth was a man who had been in the booth before. The third time, or the fourth. He had his Thursdays the way she had hers. He paid the way he had paid the first time; he came in at the count he came in at and left at the count he left at. She did not have to read him anymore. She had read him already. The hour tonight would be the hour he had shown up to buy, and she had the number that corresponded before she walked to the booth.</p> <</if>><p>She closed the till at eleven-oh-five. The front lights had been off since eleven; the sign on the door since ten-fifty. The key went into her pocket. The back-booth lamp she turned on the way she had learned to turn it on — twist-and-hold-for-the-count-of-three until the filament caught, then release. Cookie had gone home at ten-forty with the kids. Marge had locked the back door from the inside and left the key on the hook where the key went on Thursdays. The diner was hers for the hour.</p><p>The man in the booth looked up at the count he looked up at. She had the count. She had learned to read the count off a man's hand before she had learned to read the look off his face. She sat down across from him or she did not, depending on what the man had done in the sixty seconds since she had come around the counter. Each Thursday was one Thursday. Each man was one man. Each scene was one decision at a time, and she was the one making it. The decisions had stopped carrying over from one Thursday into the next. Thursday was one Thursday. Sunday she would buy groceries with the money. That was all the carry-over was.</p><p>The man tonight had done the thing the men who came to the back booth did or he had done a different thing. He came with a number and waited for her to accept it, or he came without a number and waited for her to set one. The Thursday was his Thursday and the hour was hers. He looked up at her at the count. The look at the count was the look that carried the information she needed. The look told her which of the three sentences she would say at the corner of the booth.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>Frank knew on Thursdays. Frank had known since the third Thursday in the month he had first known. He had not said the sentence that would have named the knowing and she did not expect him to. The Friday ten-twenty office ritual held and the Thursday ten-PM back booth sat on the other side of the week from it, and between them was the Friday-morning silence at the breakfast table that Diana filled the way Diana filled silences. The ritual on both sides held because the silence in the middle held.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_keep_route", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>The route she had taken on the first Sunday of the last week of July was a route she had taken. The taking held. The Thursday back booth sat inside the route in the way the Thursday back booth always had. She was not on the route because of what the Thursday back booth paid; the Thursday back booth was on the route because of what she had already decided about the shape of the route. The arithmetic ran forward now. It ran toward the first Monday of September and the number she had written down for Millhaven Community College in the line on the application she had already filled out.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "9ce04b4d-c962-4ff7-9b6d-e1b80a7f5c70">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "87e63876-77a7-4932-93cd-8d6d90ee79c3">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("9ce04b4d-c962-4ff7-9b6d-e1b80a7f5c70");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_diner_t3.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_diner_t3.base"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Stand. \"Not tonight.\" Walk to the back."
