Fluorescent strip light over the pass; late-day southern-small-town wash.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=small-town+Southern+diner+evening+interior+counter+stools+Bunn+coffee+maker+fluorescent+light&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fdiner_t0.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 small-town Southern diner evening interior counter stools Bunn coffee maker fluorescent light</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=1980s-style+American+diner+waitress+white+apron+coffee+carafe+behind+counter+booth&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fdiner_t0.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 1980s-style American diner waitress white apron coffee carafe behind counter booth</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=roadside+diner+late+shift+warmer+plate+coffee+pot+Coca-Cola+wall+clock&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fdiner_t0.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 roadside diner late shift warmer plate coffee pot Coca-Cola wall clock</a></div></div><<set _bp to random(0, 4)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>Monday slow. The church couple in booth three splitting a slice of pie and a coffee between them, the trucker at the counter with the crossword folded into quarters, Cookie on the back step between rushes — the back door propped with the brick that had been propping it since Marge bought the building in 1991.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Tuesday steady. Pete the mechanic in the booth second-from-the-end, dark-blue coveralls clean at the cuffs, the Hayes Hardware cap on the chair beside him. The retired farmer's wife at the counter. Chicken-fried steak with the gravy on the side, the way she had been ordering it since August.</p> <<elseif _bp is 2>> <p>Wednesday pickup. The shift where the dinner rush actually felt like a rush — three booths filled by 5:45, the fryer running through a second basket of potatoes, Cookie's hands steady through all of it. The Bunn knocked itself twice on the warmer plate between the second and the third refill of booth four.</p> <<elseif _bp is 3>> <p>Thursday trucker-heavy. Three rigs in the gravel turnout across the road, four men at the counter, the jukebox playing a song older than the year. The Bunn on the second warmer running because the first was running past the cut-off hour the dial-clock behind the till said it should.</p> <<else>> <p>Friday the full floor. Every booth, every two-top, the fryer running longer than it should. Marge in the back doing a quick inventory between orders — apron tied tight the way she tied it on the nights the count ran long, the till-key on the chain at her wrist.</p> <</if>><p>The apron went around her hip in the half-bow Cookie had shown her on Wednesday of Week 1 — strings crossed at the small of the back, knotted once at the front, ends tucked. The booth numbers ran counterclockwise the way the floor sloped toward the kitchen wall. The smell was coffee and bacon and Pine-Sol, the fryer grease bleeding through the swinging door from the back. Her t-shirt at the shoulders already held the two-day smell the diner put into the cotton regardless of when the shirt had last been washed.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "cookie_peer_established", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>Cookie moved through the line fast and did not waste words. Marge at the till kept her eyes on the credit slips unless there was something to keep them on. The back step had the count of Cookie's smoke breaks in a row of short-butt cigarettes along the far corner of the bottom tread, and Cookie had not, yet, offered Maya one of them. That had been the register of the first two weeks. She was inside the building. She was not yet of the building.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "cookie_peer_established", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>Cookie tipped her chin at the back step between the dinner-rush lull and the second wind. The second cigarette of the break was Maya's without Cookie having asked whether she wanted it, which was Cookie's way. Maya took it and did not smoke it and held it between two fingers the way she had watched Cookie hold the tongs.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/cookie.jpg" alt="Cookie" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Cookie:</strong> Trucker at the end. Caterpillar cap. Rounds to twenty on a twelve-dollar check if you stand by his shoulder once. Three swings from carafe to cup meant the cup was half — the count Cookie had taught her without saying so on her second night, and in the weeks since she had not found a reason to count differently. The second-cup men at the counter were the men who stayed past seven: the crossword trucker, the retired farmer, the man in the Caterpillar cap who had been at the end of the counter some number of Wednesdays, not all, a number she had not started counting yet. She had registered their hands.</p><p>Some time after eight-thirty the man in the Caterpillar cap lifted his cup and did not hold it out to be refilled. She came around with the carafe. She stopped at his right elbow. He looked up. The look was a beat longer than the look of a man being refilled by a waitress and half a beat shorter than the look she had counted on the Wednesday of Week 1 — a look she had not counted again and did not yet, she understood, know what to do with.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "cabd9584-eeb9-4513-b9b8-f349aa767d30">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "a9ea511a-6229-4278-87c2-f4502aacf780">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_marge_diner_shift.distance") === -1) { vn.push("activity_marge_diner_shift.distance"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Hold the eye a beat. "Location_Diner_Front_Floor">><<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];<</script>><<script>>setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "money", "add", 45.0, false, null);<</script>><<script>>setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "rep_road", "add", 2.0, false, null);<</script>><<script>>setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>><<script>>advanceTime(300);<</script>><</link>><br> <</nobr>><div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> Diner Shift <span style="opacity:0.7;">(activity_marge_diner_shift)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> Play Along</div> <p>The apron at her hip was the second one of the week; Cookie had flagged the one she had been wearing Monday for the Pine-Sol stain at the front-left pocket and had handed her a fresh one at the start of the shift without the sentence that would have been the handing-her-a-fresh-one. The tip jar at the end of the counter had been moved three inches closer to the cash register since her first week — she had noticed that at the beginning of August and had not, to herself, decided whether the moving had been Marge's or Cookie's or her own habit.</p><p>Pete's second cup had been in front of him long enough that the coffee in it would be past warm by the time he got to the bottom of it. She had waited the count. She had come around with the carafe at the count she had been taught by the Friday three weeks ago when Pete had finally said it out loud — <em>Maya. I take it when I'm ready.</em> He had said it once without the stress and once with. She had been watching the clock on it anyway, since. She watched differently now — she watched to time the come-around so it landed the beat Pete had given her the permission to land.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "ryan_beach_proposal", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>The joke was the one about the tourist who had asked the farmer for directions to Nashville and the farmer had answered in a sentence that did not contain Nashville. She had heard it from Cookie first, from the crossword-trucker second, from Pete-at-the-counter third, and she had laughed at it the third time too because the third laugh was the one that paid. She let herself laugh. She registered the letting. The letting was the part she had been getting used to.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "player", "trait_key": "rep_road", "operator": "gte", "value": 30}]})>> <p>A five-dollar bill under the plate at booth two. The man at booth two had been the man at booth two on three of the last four Fridays and had never left more than the twenty-percent the arithmetic of his check suggested. The five was over the twenty-percent by the count of three dollars and the count of three dollars was the count of the beat Maya had held at his elbow while she had been refilling his wife's decaf. The church couple nodded the way the church couple nodded and did not say anything.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "player", "trait_key": "rep_church", "operator": "lte", "value": 10}]})>> <p>The church couple was not in booth three tonight. They were in booth six, the one by the bathrooms, which she had set for them twice already on earlier Fridays and had both times thought the setting was for customers who had specifically asked. They had not asked tonight. The pastor's wife had walked past booth three and the woman already sitting in booth six had stood up to take her check to the counter, and the pastor's wife had taken booth six without having to request it. The tip was there at the end. The tip was the same it had been.</p> <</if>><p>Pete at the counter did the thing he did when he was ready for the refill but did not want to be the one who asked. His hand at the cup did not quite move. His shoulder shifted an inch toward the carafe she was holding. The jukebox was between songs. She had the count.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "cabd9584-eeb9-4513-b9b8-f349aa767d30">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "da084bd5-80ab-45b5-b313-f59a7971d3ef">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_marge_diner_shift.play_along") === -1) { vn.push("activity_marge_diner_shift.play_along"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Linger at his shoulder. "Location_Diner_Front_Floor">><<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];<</script>><<script>>setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "money", "add", 53.0, false, null);<</script>><<script>>setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "rep_road", "add", 2.0, false, null);<</script>><<script>>setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>><<script>>advanceTime(300);<</script>><</link>><br> <</nobr>><div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> Diner Shift <span style="opacity:0.7;">(activity_marge_diner_shift)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> Work the Floor</div> <p>The apron was the blue apron. She had bought it with the first week's tips she did not count into the rent envelope — the apron Cookie had eyed without saying anything the Wednesday Maya had put it on for the first time, the eying that had been the answer Cookie did not need to put into words. The apron had the front-pocket shape of a pocket that had held bills since June and did not un-shape itself between washes. She wore it now on the T2 shifts. The T2 shifts were hers. The T1 shifts had been the first count; the T2 shifts were the count she had come to take.</p><p>She worked the counter three rows deep. She read the room at the pass. She had her tables — two, four, six on the odd-rotation nights; one, three, five on the even — the numbering she had worked out with Cookie in the second month when Cookie had stopped handing her the tickets in the order they came up and had started handing her the ones from the tables where she would earn the most for the walk. Cookie did not say Maya was earning more. Cookie said <em>these are yours</em>. Maya took them. The taking had become the thing she did without the second-guessing. The second-guessing had been the summer's first register and was not the summer's current register.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "ryan_beach_proposal", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>The trucker at the counter was not Pete tonight — Pete was Tuesdays. The trucker was the younger one with the crew who had come in Tuesday of last week and again tonight, first at the counter this time instead of the long table. He had looked at her once when she set the placemat. She had the count of his look. She would lean on the counter at the count he was at the bottom of the coffee. The tip jar at the end of the counter was audible by eight.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "ryan_beach_proposal", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>The trucker crowd knew Ryan. She had not expected that. The crew of five at the long table had bought a flatbed off Ryan's lot in April, the scrapper at the counter had been at the shop twice this month, Pete was Pete. Half the counter asked without asking — the eye-contact on her that was a beat longer than the eye-contact on a waitress from a man who did not know the waitress was partnered with the man who had sold him his truck. She had the answer to the question they were not asking. She had not yet picked which answer to give on which night. The not-picking was the register she had not been in before and did not plan to stay in for long.</p> <</if>><p>By eight-forty the floor had the shape it had been going to have by eight. The counter was three men deep. Cookie at the pass kept the tickets coming. Maya had her tap — the second carafe on the warmer, the blue apron in the front-pocket shape it took at this weight of tips, the count of the counter she had by now done three times that evening. She knew the eye-count on her from each man at the counter. She knew which of the six was the high-tipper by the hand-on-cup and which was the mid-tipper by the way he did not quite turn his shoulder when she came past. The question was not whether to tilt the room. The question was which Maya she was going to be for the last hour.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "cabd9584-eeb9-4513-b9b8-f349aa767d30">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "258b07b0-9179-4c91-b27e-d2fbbf71fb31">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_marge_diner_shift.work_floor") === -1) { vn.push("activity_marge_diner_shift.work_floor"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Tilt the room. Long wooden table running parallel to the porch rail under a string of lights along the rafter. Five place settings, the table set for Frank, Diana, Ryan, Jake, and Maya. Frank standing at the grill at the far end of the porch in an apron, tongs in hand. Diana carrying a covered tray out from the screen door. The yard beyond — cut grass, the start of the pine line, the dirt road past the property edge. Late-summer Southern evening light, the cicadas implied by the season. The brochure was on the carpet between them, open to the art-department section, the section he had bookmarked with the corner of an envelope from the bank. He read the bullet points aloud at the volume of a person who had read brochures aloud before — Drawing I, Drawing II, Anatomy for Artists, Gallery Practicum, the visiting-artist series. He read the page in the order it had been written and stopped exactly where the page-break broke before the tuition table.</p><p>He did not say tuition. He did not flip the page. He set the brochure where it had been, with the corner of the envelope holding the page open at the curriculum side, and he picked up his sketchbook from the floor next to him and drew for a beat without saying anything else, and the saying-nothing-else was the way he said the part of the page he was not going to read aloud.</p><p>Maya did not ask him to read the page he was not going to read. The catalogued-and-left was the agreement they had not named. The naming would have been the thing that made it untrue.</p><p>She had taken the brochure home from the campus visitor center the Wednesday before and had set it on her bed and had not opened it for two days. Jake had opened it. Jake had read it. Jake had put a corner of an envelope at the curriculum-side page break. Saturated-band Maya-interior pre-arrival moment from 1:45 PM to 2:00 PM — the ledger open at customer desk, the sale sheets in the stack they went in, the receipts-pad in the drawer with the new roll of paper, the Saturday-quiet particular to a room expecting someone at 2:00. Ryan in the work bay with rolling door halfway up, the socket in his hand turning in the slow count he held when not in a hurry, cold grease and metal-rubber smell drifting on the half-light from the bay. Maya-body: jeans that fit, shirt the color of the inside of a pine board, hair back in a pencil pulled off the counter, mirror-stopped-being-a-thing-she-consulted Saturated specimen. The customer has not arrived yet — the canvas stages the WAITING, not the scene. R8 delegates full scene beats (customer arrival + price-dance + back-office close + aftermath) to the Phase-2 story canvas ryan_big_ticket_deal (B18, Session 12 rewrite). Southern-summer Saturday rural-shop pre-arrival Saturated-band inhabited-routine register.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=rural+equipment+shop+customer+area+Saturday+afternoon+empty+waiting+young+woman+ledger+counter+Southern&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fshop_big.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 rural equipment shop customer area Saturday afternoon empty waiting young woman ledger counter Southern</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=small-engine+parts+shop+Saturday+quiet+afternoon+young+woman+at+customer+desk+pre-arrival+Southern+summer&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fshop_big.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 small-engine parts shop Saturday quiet afternoon young woman at customer desk pre-arrival Southern summer</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=rural+shop+interior+Saturday+afternoon+young+woman+at+counter+with+ledger+open+waiting+for+customer&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fshop_big.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 rural shop interior Saturday afternoon young woman at counter with ledger open waiting for customer</a></div></div><p>One-forty-five in the afternoon. The ledger open at the customer desk. The sale sheets in the stack they went in. The receipts-pad in the drawer with the new roll of paper Ryan had loaded on a Wednesday. Nothing left to stage. The shop had its Saturday quiet on it — the particular quiet of a room that expected someone at two o'clock and was spending the time between then and now holding the expectation in the middle of itself without saying anything about the holding.</p><p>At one-thirty she had done what she did on Saturdays. Turned the sign to OPEN even though the sign did not strictly need turning. Ran the dust-rag along the top of the customer desk. Took the receipts for the week out of the clip and put them in the banded stack they went in. Set the ledger at the specific angle she set it at, so that whoever walked in would see the page without seeing the numbers. She had done these things without deciding to do them, because Saturday-at-one-thirty was not a time she made decisions in.</p><p>She had been ready for this Saturday for three Saturdays. She had closed smaller rooms on the two before this one — one at forty over asking, one at sixty — and the smaller rooms had been the same room at different scales. She knew the scale of the afternoon the way she knew the count on the tip jar at the end of a trucker shift without counting. The customer had been told about her without being told. Word circulated in the way words circulated in a county the size of this one. She had stopped being surprised by what circulated and what did not.</p><p>Ryan was in the work bay with the rolling door halfway up, and the smell that came in on the half-light from that direction was the smell of cold grease and the metal-and-rubber smell of an engine that had been run in the morning and was cooling. The socket in his hand was turning in the slow count he held when he was not in a hurry about anything. Past her shoulder the office door was the door it was on Saturdays — unlocked, the blind inside already down.</p><p>She had worn the jeans that fit and a shirt the color of the inside of a pine board. The hair was back in a pencil she had pulled off the counter. The color in her face was the color that came on from the summer itself. She had not looked in the bathroom mirror at Frank's house before she left, and she had not needed to. The mirror had stopped being a thing she consulted some weeks ago. The face she had at thirty would be different from the face she had now, and she was going to be ready for both.</p><p>The afternoon held. She let it hold. Fifty was the number Ryan would have called the farmer-fold — the twenty-over a man paid when he had been told a number and had read the telling and had decided that the telling was worth the twenty. Sixty was the number a man signed his name under without knowing that thirty had been on the tag and that the thirty had become something else between his walking in and his walking out.</p><p>Ryan was in the work bay. Rotating jobs week-to-week: porch rail painting, fence-line tightening along the back pasture, barn-side light bulbs, gutter clearing, mower-blade maintenance. Frank in his work belt (hammer loop on left, he&#x27;s right-handed). Maya in a t-shirt she doesn&#x27;t mind marking. Yard heat. Pine-resin smell. Cicadas through the afternoon.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=rural+property+weekend+repairs+stepfather+stepdaughter+Saturday+afternoon+outdoor+labor&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fweekend_repairs.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 rural property weekend repairs stepfather stepdaughter Saturday afternoon outdoor labor</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=Southern+farm+property+fence+porch+barn-side+work+summer+heat+afternoon+two-person+labor&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fweekend_repairs.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 Southern farm property fence porch barn-side work summer heat afternoon two-person labor</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=1970s-style+American+farm+repair+afternoon+father+daughter+figure+shared+labor+Southern+summer&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fweekend_repairs.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 1970s-style American farm repair afternoon father daughter figure shared labor Southern summer</a></div></div><p>The property at one in the afternoon was the work the property carried on the weekend. Paint on the porch rail some Saturdays. The fence line along the back pasture other Saturdays. The barn-side lights or the gutter or the mower-blade some other Saturdays. Frank wore the belt he had worn when Maya arrived — the one with the hammer loop on the left because he was right-handed and reached across. She wore the t-shirt she did not mind getting drywall dust on. The yard heat. The pine-resin smell. Cicadas.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_restrict_declared", "operator": "is_false"}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>Shared labor. No one narrated who did what. He handed her the wrench when he needed the wrench handed to him. She held the board at the end when he needed the board held. The rhythm was the rhythm two people fell into when they worked a house together and neither one of them was the boss of the house. He took water breaks at the count she had learned was his water-break count. She took hers at his. The porch rail got painted or the fence got tightened or the gutter got cleared, and the afternoon got used up in the way afternoons on the property got used up.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "npc", "npc_id": "npc_frank", "trait_key": "trust", "operator": "gte", "value": 60}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He showed her how to set the nail-head flush the way he had set nail-heads on cedar for forty years — the angle of the hammer at the last strike, the way the wrist stopped before the head met the wood. She tried. She missed. She tried again. She got it on the third strike. He did not say good this time because this time the hammer had said it. The afternoon ran through the work. She had sawdust in her hair that she did not notice until she was on the porch at the end. Frank noticed it before she did and did not tell her.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_restrict_declared", "operator": "is_true"}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>Frank had his task and she had hers. The task she had was the one he had assigned on Sunday the week before, at breakfast with Diana at the stove — paint the porch rail on Saturday, tighten the fence where the cow had pushed through on Sunday, the list that was the weekly list since the rule. They worked on the same property not on the same job. He was down at the fence. She was on the porch. The rail was the rail she had painted two coats on by three. He did not come up to check. The work was the work the list had named.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>The work the property carried on the weekend was still the work the property carried. Frank's belt was still the belt. Her t-shirt still did not mind the dust. He took his water breaks at his count. She took hers at his. The porch rail still got painted. The fence still got tightened. The afternoon got used up in the way afternoons on the property got used up after the Thursday in the office, which was the same way afternoons got used up before it, because the work did not know what had happened and the work did not need to.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "17112760-36d2-4634-8468-a965e6f1b49d">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "318983e2-b2db-4379-af40-bd98358776f6">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("17112760-36d2-4634-8468-a965e6f1b49d");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_weekend_repairs.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_weekend_repairs.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(180);<</script>> <<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "fitness", "add", 1.0, false, null);setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("npc", "npc_frank", "trust", "add", 1.0, false, null);setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>> [[Shower.->Location_Frank's_Property]] <<else>> <div class="cost-blocked-message"> <p><<= setup.getCostBlockedMessage(_costs)>></p> </div> [[Back->Location_Frank's_Property]] <</if>><<set _costs to [{"trait": "energy", "value": 20}]>>\ <<if setup.checkCostsAffordable(_costs)>>\ <<script>>setup.deductCosts("1a260f21-2211-4b91-9cf4-0300bc9d797e");<</script>> <div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> Saturday hardware run <span style="opacity:0.7;">(activity_hardware_run)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> Truck Cab</div> <div style="border:2px dashed #666;padding:20px;margin:10px 0;border-radius:8px;background:#f5f5f5;"><p style="margin:0;font-weight:bold;color:#333;">[IMAGE MISSING] activities/hardware_run.jpg</p><p style="margin:5px 0 0;color:#666;font-style:italic;">Saturday 08:00-10:00 truck run. Frank at the wheel of his pickup, Maya in the passenger seat. Bench seat with cracked vinyl, an old hand towel wadded under the seat, his travel coffee-mug between them. AM country-station radio on. Visor flipped down on Maya&#x27;s side. Route: farmhouse driveway → State Route 9 → Main Street (ninety-second stoplight) → general store at the far end → gas station → home. Two-hour round trip, confined two-person.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=pickup+truck+cab+rural+Southern+Saturday+morning+bench+seat+AM+radio+stepfather+driving&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fhardware_run.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 pickup truck cab rural Southern Saturday morning bench seat AM radio stepfather driving</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=1970s-style+American+pickup+interior+cracked+vinyl+bench+seat+travel+coffee+mug+visor+country+road&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fhardware_run.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 1970s-style American pickup interior cracked vinyl bench seat travel coffee mug visor country road</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=Southern+small-town+main+street+brick+storefronts+pickup+truck+Saturday+morning+hardware+general+store&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fhardware_run.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 Southern small-town main street brick storefronts pickup truck Saturday morning hardware general store</a></div></div><p>The truck was the one he kept because he kept the things that worked. Bench seat, cracked vinyl at the seam where the driver had worn it through, an old hand towel wadded under the bench for the coffee he spilled some weeks when he was rushing. The AM radio set to the country station out of Columbus. The visor flipped down on her side before she climbed in — he had flipped it the first week because the morning sun came through that side of the windshield on the run into town. State Route 9 into Millhaven. The stoplight at Main Street. Ninety seconds on red.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "npc", "npc_id": "npc_frank", "trait_key": "trust", "operator": "lt", "value": 30}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He drove at the speed he drove and did not change the station. She read the town going past the window because reading the town was easier than talking. The grain elevator at the turn. The water tower with the painted year. The new Shell sign at the station that the old hand-lettered sign had been replaced by in March. He parked in the three-space gravel lot beside the general store. He got out. She got out. He held the door for her at the store and he held the door for her when they came back out with the lumber and the bag of finishing nails, and he did not say why he was holding the door, and she did not ask.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "npc", "npc_id": "npc_frank", "trait_key": "trust", "operator": "gte", "value": 30}, {"type": "trait", "subject": "npc", "npc_id": "npc_frank", "trait_key": "trust", "operator": "lt", "value": 60}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He told her what he was after before they parked. Two eight-foot pieces of one-by-four for the trim on the barn and a box of galvanized nails in the length he used for cedar so the head sat flush when he set it. He said one-by-four the way Maya had heard Cookie say eggs-over-medium — the naming-of-the-thing-by-the-spec-of-the-thing. She helped him load the truck bed. He held the passenger door for her on the way in and on the way out.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/frank.jpg" alt="Frank" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong><<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>>:</strong> Thank you.</div></div><p>He said it at the count she had not expected it to come at.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "npc", "npc_id": "npc_frank", "trait_key": "trust", "operator": "gte", "value": 60}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He asked her about the sketchbook on the way out of town. He asked the way he asked the weather — without turning his head — but the asking landed heavier because the sketchbook was not a thing she had mentioned, and he had not asked about it before.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/frank.jpg" alt="Frank" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong><<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>>:</strong> What is it you draw, Maya?</div></div><p>She told him it was hands, mostly. She did not tell him whose hands. He nodded the nod that meant he had heard the part she had said and the part she had not said. The country station was between songs. The stoplight turned green. He drove.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>The truck was the same truck. The bench seat, the towel under the bench, the coffee in his travel cup, the AM country station that nobody turned off. He drove at the speed he drove. She read the town going past the window because reading the town was still easier than talking. The Saturday-morning hardware run had been the run before the Thursday and was the run after it, and the run held because the run was a run and the Ford held air and they had gone to pick up what they had gone to pick up.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "1a260f21-2211-4b91-9cf4-0300bc9d797e">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "1965826c-d1d4-4db8-98a7-154503e78793">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("1a260f21-2211-4b91-9cf4-0300bc9d797e");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_hardware_run.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_hardware_run.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(120);<</script>> <<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("npc", "npc_frank", "trust", "add", 2.0, false, null);setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>> [[Climb out. Unload the bed.->Location_Driveway_/_Town-Walk_Path]] <<else>> <div class="cost-blocked-message"> <p><<= setup.getCostBlockedMessage(_costs)>></p> </div> [[Back->Location_Driveway_/_Town-Walk_Path]] <</if>><<set _costs to [{"trait": "energy", "value": 5}]>>\ <<if setup.checkCostsAffordable(_costs)>>\ <<script>>setup.deductCosts("1af89b65-0853-4561-86da-9fcab5f91137");<</script>> <div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> Porch evening with Frank <span style="opacity:0.7;">(activity_porch_frank)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> Porch</div> <img src="./videos/activities/porch_frank.jpg" alt="" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="max-width:100%;max-height:70vh;object-fit:contain;height:auto;border-radius:8px;" /><p>The front porch at nine in the evening had two rocking chairs and a small table between them with Frank's ashtray from before he stopped smoking in eighty-three and the bottle of whiskey he kept out there in the summer because Diana did not keep liquor in the kitchen. The porch light was the light Frank kept off after midnight. The screen door was the sound of the house. The yard was dark past the reach of the porch. Cicadas.</p><<set _bp to random(0, 3)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>Whiskey and silence. He had poured two fingers into his own glass and a finger into hers because she had not finished the glass he had poured the last time. The cicadas were negotiating something at the end of the yard. He rocked at a slow count. She rocked at a count close to his but not the same. He said nothing. He was not going to. The silence was the sentence.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Whiskey and a question he asked about her day without looking at her.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/frank.jpg" alt="Frank" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong><<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>>:</strong> How's Marge treating you?</div></div><p>He asked the way he asked the weather. He did not turn his head. The ice in his glass had gotten to the top. He poured the whiskey fresh over it. She told him about the Wednesday the Caterpillar-cap man had tipped her fifteen on a six-dollar check, and he nodded the nod he nodded when the Ford had held air six weeks longer than it had any right to.</p> <<elseif _bp is 2>> <p>Whiskey and Diana on the phone in the kitchen behind them, the screen door holding the sound in the way the screen door held any sound not loud enough to come through it. Diana was talking to her sister in Georgia — the cousin she would not stop apologizing for, the boy the cousin had married, the new roof on the house they should not have bought. Frank listened without listening. She listened without listening. The porch was the porch.</p> <<else>> <p>Whiskey and the porch light going off early. He had set the bottle on the table. He had not refilled his glass or hers. He pulled the chain at the overhead bulb with the second finger of his right hand the way he always pulled it, and the porch went from yellow to the blue of the yard-dark.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/frank.jpg" alt="Frank" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong><<print $npcs["1e5b4a6f-d7d3-4495-bd4f-32131c454a8d"].name>>:</strong> Goodnight, Maya.</div></div><p>The screen door closed behind him at the count the screen door closed at.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "1af89b65-0853-4561-86da-9fcab5f91137">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "65b79d3e-44dc-4424-9fcb-8d0272ad0e62">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("1af89b65-0853-4561-86da-9fcab5f91137");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_porch_frank.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_porch_frank.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(60);<</script>> <<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("npc", "npc_frank", "trust", "add", 1.0, false, null);setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>> [[Inside.->Location_Front_Porch]] <<else>> <div class="cost-blocked-message"> <p><<= setup.getCostBlockedMessage(_costs)>></p> </div> [[Back->Location_Front_Porch]] <</if>><<set _costs to [{"trait": "energy", "value": 15}]>>\ <<if setup.checkCostsAffordable(_costs)>>\ <<script>>setup.deductCosts("b26247fa-e034-40e0-9cc8-491681f6f329");<</script>> <div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> Help with bookkeeping <span style="opacity:0.7;">(activity_bookkeeping)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> The Ledger</div> <img src="./videos/activities/bookkeeping.jpg" alt="" loading="lazy" decoding="async" style="max-width:100%;max-height:70vh;object-fit:contain;height:auto;border-radius:8px;" /><p>Frank's office at eight in the evening was a small room with a desk facing the window so he could see the yard while he worked. The amber lamp had been on the desk before Maya moved in. The ledger was open to the week. The pencil had its eraser worn down to the metal ferrule. The envelope of Friday's receipts sat on the corner of the desk where Frank had put it after dinner. The metal filing cabinets along the wall were older than the house. The window to the porch cracked open so the crickets came in. The door was open — the door was always open in the office when she was in it.</p><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_restrict_declared", "operator": "is_false"}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He slid the ledger halfway across the desk so she could work from her chair. The week's small columns. A figure at the top of the third column she caught before she had set her pencil down — a transposed forty-seven for seventy-four in the feed-store line, the kind of mistake Frank did not make. She made the correction. He watched her make it. He did not say it was a test and he did not thank her for the catch. He turned the page and pointed to the next column with the blunt end of his pen. The discipline was in the error he had left for her and in the saying-nothing about either the error or the catch.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "trait", "subject": "npc", "npc_id": "npc_frank", "trait_key": "trust", "operator": "gte", "value": 60}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He stood to lean past her at the column and his shoulder came against hers and stayed there one beat longer than leaning-over-a-column needed. His other hand went flat on the desk to her right. The amber lamp was warm on both their hands. He did not move the shoulder away. He pointed at the figure and his finger stopped on the paper and stayed. She kept her pencil on the column. He moved back to his chair at the count he had been moving back by since the second week of June.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "logic": "AND", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_tease_under_compliance_open", "operator": "is_true"}, {"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_false"}]})>> <p>He stood to lean past her at the column. She did not move away from the lean. The rule was that the door stayed open and the rule was that they worked on the ledger and the rule had not named the space between her chair and his desk. Her chair was the chair she had pulled across the floor on her first week. His hand was flat on the desk to her right. The crickets at the porch came through the window. He turned the page when the page was done. Nothing was said about the lean and nothing needed to be said.</p> <<elseif setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_cracked", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>Neither of them pretended it was about the ledger. Somebody before her had got this far and stopped, and the somebody-before-her was likely Diana, in a different summer, deciding the same thing about the book.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>The college brochure folded back to the financial-aid page that did not get shorter the more times she read it. Pavement cooling under her sneakers, the asphalt giving back the day's heat in a way the morning road never did. Shadows long sideways across the road. Cicadas still at it, the volume that meant the sun was on the way down but had not yet committed. She walked the middle of the lane because she could.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Dusk, the kudzu side. A pickup went by the other way and she did not turn her head to look. She had been getting tired of turning to look the way a person got tired of looking up to check that a clock had not changed in the last minute. Her sneakers had a layer of red dust now they had not had a year ago. The truck did not slow.</p> <<elseif _bp is 2>> <p>Late evening. By the time the road curved past Ryan's shop the truck was back and the shop's roll-up door was down — Ryan was inside the house already, the second-story light on. Porch light landed in a square on the gravel ahead of her. Diana's silhouette at the kitchen window, the shape of her cleaning a counter she had cleaned three times that day. Maya slowed her pace without meaning to. She had been doing the slow-down by the second week.</p> <<else>> <p>After two in the morning. The road dark in the way the road only got dark in the hour after the diner closed and before the early shifts started. She walked by the light of other people's porches — the Hayes place at the bend, the trailer past the post office, Frank's at the end. The cicadas were quieter at this hour, or her ears had stopped paying them.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "5ba75acf-55c0-4805-87d9-f02d92287280">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "b21817f7-669d-43f7-a1b3-9a673629fa59">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("5ba75acf-55c0-4805-87d9-f02d92287280");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_walk_home.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_walk_home.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(30);<</script>> [[Up the porch steps. Heat-haze on the asphalt distance. Mid-day Southern light, low traffic. The walk-to-town canvas covers the half-hour from loc_driveway out to loc_main_street_sidewalk.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=rural+Southern+county+road+pine+kudzu+summer+heat+haze+woman+walking+centerline+mid-day&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fwalk_to_town.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 rural Southern county road pine kudzu summer heat haze woman walking centerline mid-day</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=North+Alabama+rural+county+road+gravel-to-pavement+pine+canopy+weekday+afternoon+woman+jeans+walking&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fwalk_to_town.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 North Alabama rural county road gravel-to-pavement pine canopy weekday afternoon woman jeans walking</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=small-town+Southern+county+road+afternoon+pine+kudzu+cicadas+heat-haze+young+woman+walking+errands&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=activities%2Fwalk_to_town.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 small-town Southern county road afternoon pine kudzu cicadas heat-haze young woman walking errands</a></div></div><<set _bp to random(0, 3)>> <<if _bp is 0>> <p>Saturday morning. Gravel for fifty yards before it took the county road's pavement. Ryan's shop on the property edge, the big roll-up door pulled down — the padlock clipped through the loop the way Ryan clipped a padlock when the shop was shut for the day, not the way he clipped it for the night. The yard around the shop was empty of equipment, which meant whatever had been there yesterday had a buyer. Cicadas not yet at full volume.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Mid-morning, the kudzu side of the road. A pickup truck slowed coming the other way, then did not stop. The driver — older, ball cap pulled low, a face she had not seen before — gave her the long look, the kind of look that asked a thing without expecting an answer. Maya did not turn her head to follow the truck after it had passed. The not-turning was the answer.</p> <<elseif _bp is 2>> <p>Afternoon, second mile marker. Pine and kudzu closed over the road, heat trapped where the canopy thinned. Cicadas at full volume now, and the red clay was ticking under her sneakers — the sound it made in the heat that she had only learned to hear after the third week of walking. She made a list in her head and forgot half of it before the third bend.</p> <<else>> <p>Sunday morning, late. A car slowed coming the other way — a woman her mother's age, hair set the way her mother had set hers for church, gave the windshield-nod that meant a thing in this part of the county. Maya gave the nod back without thinking. The car kept going. The nod, Maya was learning, was a contract you signed by accident.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "d61bb200-59bb-4385-86b7-869d2ed77b29">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "02890030-c882-4294-ae70-29f9f139a117">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("d61bb200-59bb-4385-86b7-869d2ed77b29");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_walk_to_town.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_walk_to_town.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(30);<</script>> [[Step up onto the sidewalk.->Location_Main_Street_Sidewalk]] <<else>> <div class="cost-blocked-message"> <p><<= setup.getCostBlockedMessage(_costs)>></p> </div> [[Back->Location_Driveway_/_Town-Walk_Path]] <</if>><<set _costs to [{"trait": "energy", "value": 5}, {"trait": "hygiene", "value": 1}]>>\ <<if setup.checkCostsAffordable(_costs)>>\ <<script>>setup.deductCosts("30a695cc-c2d6-4d37-b99f-b2d9bd894d23");<</script>> <div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> Time at the creek <span style="opacity:0.7;">(activity_walk_creek)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> The Creek</div> <div style="border:2px dashed #666;padding:20px;margin:10px 0;border-radius:8px;background:#f5f5f5;"><p style="margin:0;font-weight:bold;color:#333;">[IMAGE MISSING] activities/walk_creek.jpg</p><p style="margin:5px 0 0;color:#666;font-style:italic;">Tier F at-creek contemplation canvas (sibling to activity_sketch_creek, deliberately sketchbook-ABSENT — this is the bridges-solo-and-swimming Maya-not-making-the-page-honest mode per priority queue &#x27;Bridges solo and swimming&#x27;). loc_creek 09:00-19:00, max_triggers_per_day=1. The creek had not warmed past the night's temperature, the way it did not warm past the night's temperature until the sun cleared the pines. Creek-mud smell — colder than mud, the way water-cooled mud kept its own register apart from the dry kind. She sat on the flat rock and put her hand into the slow-water pool, wrist-deep. The cold went up to the elbow before her body let her notice it. The dragonflies had not arrived yet.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>Mid-day, the sun finding her between the pines where the canopy let it through. The shallow part of the creek had a sand stretch that Ryan had told her — in his way of telling things by mentioning them once and never again — he had swum in as a kid. Maya watched the water move over the sand-stretch and let herself think about being in it, the temperature of being in it, the body that would be doing the being-in. She had not yet decided whether the decision was a decision.</p> <<else>> <p>Late afternoon. The flat rock had been warm under her thighs for an hour before she noticed she had been sitting on it for an hour. Cicadas in the pines and the slow-water pool's surface broken into half-light where the leaves moved. She knew Jake knew the sand stretch and did not come down to it — knew it the way she had come to know things about him in the course of being in the same house. The walk back up the trail would take twenty minutes. She gave it five more first.</p> <</if>> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "30a695cc-c2d6-4d37-b99f-b2d9bd894d23">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "c9d9215a-a7ae-469b-b3bc-9782cd7cece2">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("30a695cc-c2d6-4d37-b99f-b2d9bd894d23");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("activity_walk_creek.base") === -1) { vn.push("activity_walk_creek.base"); }<</script>> <<script>>advanceTime(30);<</script>> <<script>>setup.pendingEffects = [];setup.applyAndNotifyTrait("player", null, "fitness", "add", 1.0, false, null);setup.showEffectNotification();<</script>> [[Walk the trail back. The cicadas were not at full volume yet. The grass had taken the dew. The pines past the yard held the heat from yesterday.</p> <<elseif _bp is 1>> <p>The string lights on the back porch were on still from last night, working pointlessly against the sun. The yard's grass had the late-summer dryness Diana hosed back into it on Sundays. The dark band of the bedroom door at the bottom of the four-inch gap was not Jake's.</p> <</if>><<if setup.triggerConditionsSatisfied({"version": "1.0", "items": [{"type": "flag", "subject": "player", "flag_key": "frank_keep_romantic", "operator": "is_true"}]})>> <p>The porch light was off. The table reads as Sunday, not everyday.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=southern+sunday+dinner+kitchen+table+good+plates+blue+willow+covered+pot+enamel+late+afternoon+light&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn1_good_plates_kitchen.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 southern sunday dinner kitchen table good plates blue willow covered pot enamel late afternoon light</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=home-cooked+chicken+and+dumplings+flat+kind+sunday+dinner+southern+kitchen+five+places&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn1_good_plates_kitchen.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 home-cooked chicken and dumplings flat kind sunday dinner southern kitchen five places</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=mother+setting+sunday+table+good+china+family+close+light+through+window+summer+evening&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn1_good_plates_kitchen.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 mother setting sunday table good china family close light through window summer evening</a></div></div><p>The second Sunday in October was the Sunday Diana made the flat-dumpling chicken, which was the Sunday Maya registered the thing she had not let herself register in the five Sundays before it — that Diana had been building toward a dinner since sometime in August, and the building had been slow, and the dinner was tonight, and Maya was the one it was being built toward.</p><p>The good plates were on the table. They were the blue-willow plates that lived on the top shelf of the left cabinet, the ones Diana had not put on the table since the Easter after the move. The napkins were the cloth ones, ironed flat. The iced tea was in the pitcher Diana brought out at company, not in the plastic jug the weekday tea came in. The overhead light was off and the pendant over the table was on, and the pendant had been on since Maya had come downstairs, which meant Diana had been at the table for longer than the dumplings had needed her. The kitchen smelled of chicken broth reduced down to the color of a low amber, of black pepper cracked that afternoon and not from the shaker, of the biscuit-flour kind of dough the flat dumplings were cut from before they went into the pot. The smell was not the usual Sunday smell. The smell was the Sunday-before-the-move smell, which was the smell of a kitchen Diana had learned to run as a wife, not as a widow remarried.</p><p><em>The flat kind, not the round.</em> The sentence arrived at the volume of a voice heard a long time ago in a kitchen in Tennessee. Maya's father had said it every Sunday he had been able to say it, which had been the Sundays of her first eight years, and the saying had been part of the requesting and the requesting had been part of the routine, and the routine had ended on a Wednesday in her ninth year and had not been reassembled until this Sunday in this kitchen by this woman at this table. The flat kind, not the round. Diana had made them flat. Diana had cut the dough in strips with a knife and not with a glass. Diana had remembered.</p><p>Frank was at the foot of the table. Ryan was in the chair he always sat in on the brothers' side, the one closer to Frank. Jake was in the chair closer to where Diana would sit, which was the chair at the head. The fifth chair was the chair across from Jake, which was the chair Maya had sat in every Sunday since the second Sunday of August. It was pulled out. It was not the chair the extra place setting was at.</p><p>The extra place setting was next to Diana's, on Diana's right, where the empty chair from the extra leaf of the table had been pulled up. The blue-willow plate at that place was face-up. The flatware was aligned. The cloth napkin was folded in thirds. The chair had been pulled out for her.</p><p>Diana came from the stove with the pot and set it at the trivet at the center of the table. She straightened. She wiped her palms on the apron. She looked at Maya — not at the face, at the hand Maya had on the back of the chair Maya had been standing behind for forty seconds without sitting.</p><div class="dialog-block dialog-npc"><div class="portrait"><img src="./videos/diana.jpg" alt="Diana" onerror="this.style.display='none';this.parentElement.innerHTML='&lt;svg viewBox=&quot;0 0 100 100&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://www.w3.org/2000/svg&quot;&gt;&lt;circle cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;35&quot; r=&quot;20&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;ellipse cx=&quot;50&quot; cy=&quot;85&quot; rx=&quot;35&quot; ry=&quot;25&quot; fill=&quot;#6c757d&quot;/&gt;&lt;/svg&gt;';" /></div><div class="dialog-content"><strong>Diana:</strong> Maya, honey. Set a place for yourself next to me.</div></div><p>The sentence was eleven words. It was the only full sentence Diana had said to Maya about anything that was not the grocery list or the laundry or the porch since the Monday in late May when Maya had carried her suitcase in off the drive. It was the sentence Diana had not said for four and a half months. It was the sentence Diana had been not-saying since the second week of July when the Thursday hour had started, and she had been not-saying it louder with each week, and the not-saying had been a discipline, and the discipline had been what made the saying of it tonight weigh what it weighed.</p><p>Maya moved to the chair on Diana's right. She pulled it in. She sat. The chair she had been standing behind stayed empty; the chair across from Jake, which had been her summer chair, was not her chair now. Frank registered the move without looking up from the plate. Ryan registered it by putting down the glass. Jake registered it by putting the glasses in his shirt pocket the way he had put them in his shirt pocket the Saturday of the brothers-discover dinner. None of them spoke. The dinner was the dinner. The plates went around. Diana served the dumplings into each bowl with the ladle that belonged to the good serving set, which was the ladle that had not been on the table since Tennessee.</p><p>Maya ate next to Diana. Diana's arm was warm in the space between them. The food was good. Maya had forgotten that her mother had been a cook before she had been a widow, and she had forgotten that the kitchen Diana had kept in the first house had been a different kitchen with a different arithmetic, and the remembering landed on the flat dumpling on the fork between her plate and her mouth and stayed.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "eb7ebffb-31df-4294-9bcd-59c4148ae69c">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "2b74cc6c-6044-4496-b8f7-d41632011147">> <<script>>setup.markCanvasTriggered("eb7ebffb-31df-4294-9bcd-59c4148ae69c");<</script>> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("keep_tier_fork.the_dinner") === -1) { vn.push("keep_tier_fork.the_dinner"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "Finish the plate." "Canvas_keep_tier_fork_Node_2">><<script>>advanceTime(35);<</script>><</link>><br> <</nobr>><div class="dev-canvas-info"><strong>Canvas:</strong> The Fork <span style="opacity:0.7;">(keep_tier_fork)</span> | <strong>Node:</strong> The Doorway, the Coffee</div> <div style="border:2px dashed #666;padding:20px;margin:10px 0;border-radius:8px;background:#f5f5f5;"><p style="margin:0;font-weight:bold;color:#333;">[IMAGE MISSING] story/keep_tier_fork/n2_doorway_coffee.jpg</p><p style="margin:5px 0 0;color:#666;font-style:italic;">An older woman turning in a kitchen doorway to look back at the table — soft Sunday-evening light, a table with dinner plates still on it, a younger woman seated at the head end. The look is held, the older woman does not speak, the look is the question.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=mother+turning+in+kitchen+doorway+looking+back+at+table+sunday+dinner+evening+warm+light&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn2_doorway_coffee.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 mother turning in kitchen doorway looking back at table sunday dinner evening warm light</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=older+woman+at+doorway+quiet+look+to+daughter+across+family+dinner+table+fall+evening&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn2_doorway_coffee.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 older woman at doorway quiet look to daughter across family dinner table fall evening</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=charged+domestic+pause+mother+in+doorway+younger+woman+at+table+soft+pendant+light+south&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn2_doorway_coffee.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 charged domestic pause mother in doorway younger woman at table soft pendant light south</a></div></div><p>Diana finished her plate before Maya finished hers. Diana always finished her plate before Maya did; Diana ate at the weight a woman ate at when she had been cooking since the men had come in from church at noon. She pushed back from the chair. She picked up her plate. She picked up Frank's plate because Frank had finished. She picked up Jake's fork because Jake had set it on the napkin. She did not pick up Ryan's plate because Ryan was still eating.</p><p>She carried the plates through the arch between the table and the kitchen. The kitchen was three steps in. The percolator was on the counter next to the stove. The can of Maxwell House was open on the counter next to the percolator. Diana set the plates in the sink, not on the counter. She ran the tap for a second, not for rinsing — the running-for-a-second was the signal to the table that the dishes had not been started yet, they were going to sit a minute — and she went to the percolator.</p><p>She turned in the doorway before she went to the percolator. She stood in the kitchen doorway and she looked at Maya. She did not smile. She did not frown. She did not say anything. She held the look for the count of three, which was the count past polite by two counts, which was the count Diana did not hold a look for, which was a count Diana had not held a look for since June.</p><p>Then she turned back into the kitchen and the percolator came on and the water ran for real this time and the can of Maxwell House got opened the rest of the way and the scoop went into the grounds and the grounds went into the basket and the basket went into the percolator. The sounds were the sounds. The sounds were the sounds of a mother making coffee for two cups, because the Sunday coffee after dinner was Diana and Frank and Frank did not drink coffee after Sunday dinner unless Diana had made it for two cups specifically, which was the Sundays Diana wanted the second cup for herself.</p><p>The look had been the question Diana had not asked all summer. The question she did not want the answer to had become — at some hour of some day Maya had not been counting — the question Diana had decided she did want the answer to, and the wanting had become a thing Diana had been holding behind her not-asking, and the holding had filled up until the holding could not hold anymore, and the not-asking had come out on a Sunday night through the Maxwell House and the ironed napkin and the chair on her right and a single sentence said in daylight at a volume anyone at the table could hear, and then the not-asking had put itself back on — as the look, which was the form of the question when the woman asking it was Diana.</p><p>Frank did not stand. Ryan did not stand. Jake did not stand. The three men at the table were waiting to see what Maya did next, and each of them had a stake in what she did next, and each of them was sitting in the chair he was sitting in at the weight his stake put him at. Diana was in the kitchen making coffee. Diana did not have a stake; Diana had already decided to accept whichever Maya Maya was going to be tonight, and the percolator was the shape that acceptance took while it waited.</p><p>Maya stood.</p> <<set $game_state.current_canvas = "eb7ebffb-31df-4294-9bcd-59c4148ae69c">> <<set $game_state.current_node = "0eb7227d-77e7-4067-b160-b3046773ecb7">> <<script>>var vn = State.variables.game_state.visited_nodes;if (vn.indexOf("keep_tier_fork.diana_in_the_kitchen") === -1) { vn.push("keep_tier_fork.diana_in_the_kitchen"); }<</script>> <<nobr>> <<link "To the doorway." Late-Sunday-evening light.</p><div style="margin-top:10px;"><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=woman+at+dining+room+kitchen+threshold+choosing+where+to+go+sunday+dinner+ended+southern&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn3_five_doors.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 woman at dining room kitchen threshold choosing where to go sunday dinner ended southern</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=charged+pause+threshold+between+rooms+five+destinations+possible+sunday+evening+interior&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn3_five_doors.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 charged pause threshold between rooms five destinations possible sunday evening interior</a><a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=young+woman+standing+at+transition+between+rooms+in+family+home+evening+october+light&amp;_tmc_game=output&amp;_tmc_scene=story%2Fkeep_tier_fork%2Fn3_five_doors.jpg" target="_blank" style="display:inline-block;margin:4px 8px 4px 0;padding:6px 12px;background:#3b82f6;color:white;text-decoration:none;border-radius:4px;font-size:13px;">🔍 young woman standing at transition between rooms in family home evening october light</a></div></div><p>She stood at the space between the dining room and the kitchen and saw them. She did not catalog them. The catalog was done. She saw them the way she saw the coat on the hook and the shoes by the door and the truck-keys on the hook — inhabited, arranged, inside the hour they were in.</p><p>The kitchen. The doorway she had watched Diana turn in. Three steps in, past the arch, the percolator on the counter, Diana at it with her back to the doorway. The second cup was on the counter. Diana had set it out before she had asked the scoop to go into the basket. The second cup was for Maya if Maya came through the arch now. The morning Phase 2 opened on, if this was the choice, would be the morning the two of them had the kitchen and the house, and the house would be the house the mothers had and the men were around the edges of.</p><p>The table. Frank across it. The length of it between them the way the length of the office desk had been between them on the Thursday of the Call-out. She could sit back down. She could hold his eye across the plates that had not been cleared past his side. The pendant was still on. The pendant would go off when the dishes came off the table, and the going-off would be the seal on whatever look had passed between them in the minutes before. She knew the Thursday ritual she had been walking to for seven Thursdays. She knew what the Monday-Tuesday after would be if tonight was the Frank night.</p><p>The yard. Ryan had gone out to the shop after his plate, when Diana had been clearing. The porch light was on. The screen to the back porch was closed but not latched. The shop door at the far side of the yard was closed — he was in the shop, at the tarps, at the bench. He had drunk water at dinner and not beer, and the not-beer had been a thing he had done to himself before the dinner started, on the chance of tonight. She had not given him a signal either way. He had made the not-beer choice alone. The Ryan morning was the morning after the shop, which was the morning the pickup cab was a room she was in before the diner shift.</p><p>The hall. Down past the staircase, the left hallway, Jake's room at the end. The third-floor light had been on when she came down to dinner and it had still been on when she sat. He had not looked at her at the table beyond the glasses-in-the-shirt-pocket gesture. He had been waiting the same way Ryan had been waiting, at a different weight. The Jake morning was the morning the tooth-paper had three new pages and he did not have to hide them, and she did not have to not-have-seen them.</p><p>Her own room. Up. Fourteen stairs. The door at the top of the landing, closed quietly behind her at the weight she closed doors at now. The room she had mapped with her eyes closed on her first morning and had been mapping with her eyes open for four months since. Her bed, her sketchbook on the desk, the window she had not closed because the October air was the air she had learned this summer. The Deferred morning was the morning nothing had been said to anyone, and the not-having-said would be the thing she carried into Phase 2 as its own kind of weight.</p><p>Five rooms. The five were hers. The rehearsal was over; the rehearsal had been the summer. Her body had been leaning toward one of them for a count of days now, and the count had ended some earlier hour of this Sunday, and what her body was doing in the doorway was remembering which of the five it had decided on before the dinner had started.
